user.title: Connect to the SDS200 Bridge add-on
user.description: Enter the host and port where the sds200_bridge add-on's API is reachable. Port is the add-on's *internal* port (8000 by default) -- use that even if you remapped the external port in the add-on's Network settings, that remap doesn't apply here. Host is the add-on's Supervisor hostname, which for a locally-installed add-on is NOT predictable (not just the slug, and not 'local_<slug>' either) -- on one real install it was 'aa65dcfd-sds200-bridge'. If unsure, check from a terminal on the same internal network with `curl http://<guess>:8000/scanners`, or via the Home Assistant CLI's `ha addons info sds200_bridge`.

reconfigure.title: Change the SDS200 Bridge add-on's host or port
reconfigure.description: Update where the sds200_bridge add-on's API is reachable. Port is the add-on's *internal* port (8000 by default) -- remapping the external port in the add-on's Network settings does not change it, so leave this at 8000 unless you changed main.py's HTTP_PORT. If you are connecting over the LAN by the Home Assistant host's own IP instead of the add-on's Supervisor hostname, use the *external* (remapped) port here instead.
